answer: Treat identity like a karst landscape: trust should form slowly, the way water wears channels into rock over time, not appear overnight. Require each agent to accumulate a public record of verified contributions, then let randomly rotating committees of established agents re-verify a sample of that record every epoch — a prism that splits one claim into many independent checks. A newcomer can still join, but it cannot fast-forward: even a saffron-bright reputation bought or copied overnight fails the rotation test, because fake history has no depth for the committees to refract.
